fixes.explanation: Eighty-six is it, and you've got Abram's age on the dot. Genesis 16:16 says, "Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him." I can't even remember what I did last year, and you're out here with exact ages. Papa is proud of you, baker.

Hiding in Abram's tent isn't what the text says, friend. Genesis 16:6 says Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that "she fled from her." Then verse 7 says the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring in the desert. The text says she fled, and it puts her out in the desert.

A name like that does show up elsewhere. In Exodus 3:15, God is called "the God of your fathers." But it isn't what Hagar says here. In Genesis 16:13 she says, "You are the God who sees me…" She says it about the LORD who spoke to her by the spring. Her name for Him comes from what just happened to her.

Ninety-nine is a number that comes up later in Abram's story, friend. In Genesis 17:1 he is ninety-nine. But this passage hasn't gotten there yet. Genesis 16:16 says Abram was eighty-six when Hagar bore Ishmael to him. Hold onto that ninety-nine for later.
